title: Full-stack web roadmap
tagline: From zero to a live app, with free Vietnamese video courses.
intro: Six stages, from how the web works to a deployed full-stack app. Every course is free on YouTube and in Vietnamese, with F8 first wherever it has one.
Each stage has playlists to watch and a project to build on your own. Watching without coding is the surest way to give up.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Six stages, each ending in a project you build alone.

blocks.caption: Take them in order: each stage builds on everything before it.

items.label: Basics & tools
items.detail: Learn how the web works, and use a terminal and Git before writing any code
explain: The browser sends a request, and a server answers with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Every later stage teaches you to write one of those, or the server that sends them.
The terminal is where you run npm, git and your server. On Windows, install WSL so the commands match macOS and Linux, as in the videos.
Git keeps the history of your code: commit after every session and push to GitHub. After six stages, that GitHub profile is your portfolio.

items.label: HTML & CSS
items.detail: Build static pages, then make them fit phones, tablets and desktops
explain: HTML says what a page holds: headings, paragraphs, images, forms. CSS says how it looks: colour, spacing, and layout with flexbox and grid.
Responsive means one page for many screens. A media query changes the layout by width, for example three columns on a desktop and one on a phone.
Finish the stage by building a landing page from a design image, with no video open, until it looks close to the original.

items.label: JavaScript
items.detail: Make pages respond: handle clicks and forms, call APIs, redraw from data
explain: The basics: variables, functions, arrays, objects, loops and the DOM. For example, pressing Add puts a new row in a to-do list.
The advanced part: callbacks, Promises, async/await and fetch. React and Node use them everywhere, so do not skip ahead to a framework.
A project to try: a weather app that calls a public API with fetch, shows the result and reports an error for a misspelt city.

items.label: ReactJS
items.detail: Split the interface into components and keep data in hooks, not hand-edited DOM
explain: A component is a function that returns interface, such as a ProductCard taking name and price props. A whole page is assembled from pieces like it.
useState holds data that changes; useEffect runs side work such as an API call when the component appears. These two cover most everyday React.
Start projects with Vite. Create React App, used in older videos, is no longer maintained; components, props and hooks are unchanged.

items.label: Node, Express & databases
items.detail: Write a server that takes requests, reads and writes a database, and returns JSON
explain: Express answers requests by route: GET /api/products returns the product list and POST /api/products creates a new one.
A database keeps data when the server stops. MongoDB stores JSON-like documents; MySQL and PostgreSQL store tables joined with JOIN. Know both kinds.
Signing in: the server checks the password against its hash, then returns a session cookie or a JWT so later requests know who you are.

items.label: Full-stack project & deploy
items.detail: Connect React to your own API, add sign-in, and put it online for others to use
explain: The React frontend calls the Express API with fetch, and the API reads and writes the database. CORS errors are common the first time the two run on separate ports.
Deploy the frontend to Vercel or Netlify, and the backend and database to Render, Railway or a VPS. Environment variables keep the database password out of the code.
This is the project for your CV: a working link, and a GitHub repo whose README says what the app does and how to run it.

Tự Học Next.JS Cơ Bản (với React và TypeScript)

items: TypeScript adds types to JavaScript and catches mistakes before the code runs. React and Node job posts often ask for it.
Next.js is React with routing, server rendering and an API in one project.

sections.title: How to study
sections.summary: The videos are half of it; the other half is typing it yourself.

items: Watch one lesson, close the video, and retype the code from memory before moving on.
At the end of each stage, build the checklist project with no video open. When stuck, read MDN or react.dev before rewatching.
Commit and push to GitHub after every session, even when the code is unfinished.
Keep a fixed schedule, say one to two hours a day. Steady beats cramming at the weekend.
Stuck for more than 30 minutes? Ask: say what you are doing, paste the exact error, and list what you tried.
